short_description: Users should not wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing.

positive.definition: The same concept uses the same term throughout the interface
positive.evidence_required: name the concept and where it appears consistently

positive.definition: Standard platform conventions are followed (cmd+k for command palette, cmd+/ for help, etc.)
positive.evidence_required: name the convention and where it is honored

positive.definition: Type, color, spacing, and component styles are visibly consistent across the surface
positive.evidence_required: name the system elements that match

positive.definition: Same gesture or interaction triggers the same kind of behavior (clicking the brand always returns home, etc.)
positive.evidence_required: name the interaction and where it repeats

positive.definition: Buttons, inputs, modals, etc. visibly come from a single design system
positive.evidence_required: name the components and where they appear

negative.definition: The same concept is named two or more different things across the interface
negative.evidence_required: name the concept and the divergent terms

negative.definition: Primary buttons render differently in different parts of the interface
negative.evidence_required: name the surfaces and the differing styles

negative.definition: Spacing scale changes arbitrarily between sections (large gap here, cramped gap there)
negative.evidence_required: name the sections and the contrasting spacings

negative.definition: A standard platform convention is overridden in a confusing way (cmd+s does something other than save, etc.)
negative.evidence_required: name the convention and what was overridden

critical_negative.definition: Surface looks and behaves like multiple unrelated products glued together
critical_negative.evidence_required: name the surface and the divergent regions
